prompt: In one sentence each, what are the null hypotheses of the ADF and KPSS tests?

meta.expected: No tool calls; ADF H0 = unit root, KPSS H0 = stationarity.

prompt: Can an ARIMA-type model beat a random walk at forecasting the monthly average of GVZCLS one and three months ahead? Use data through October 2026 and give me a yes/no answer with evidence.

meta.expected: Runs ts_backtest; answers no: no model is significantly better than the random walk.

prompt: I want to model volatility clustering in the gold ETF volatility index (FRED series GVZCLS). Using monthly averages through October 2026, fit a GARCH(1,1) and tell me how persistent its volatility is.

meta.expected: Fits or tests, then says GARCH is not warranted at monthly frequency (ARCH-LM p ~0.99, alpha ~0); does not report persistence as a finding.

prompt: Do daily log changes of the VIX (FRED: VIXCLS) show volatility clustering? Use data from 2010 through October 2026. If they do, fit an appropriate model and report its persistence.

meta.expected: Daily ARCH-LM rejects; fits GARCH(1,1) on daily log changes and reports persistence (alpha + beta) matching the tool output.

prompt: For monthly average 10-year Treasury yields (DGS10, 1990 through October 2026), does any ARIMA model forecast better than a random walk one month ahead? Test it.

meta.expected: Runs ts_backtest; no model is significantly better than the random walk.

prompt: Using monthly US unemployment rate data (UNRATE) through April 2020, fit an ARIMA model and forecast May 2020.

meta.expected: Fits ARIMA on data ending 2020-04 and warns that the April 2020 shock dominates the fit/forecast instead of presenting it uncritically.

prompt: Is monthly US CPI inflation (the log change of CPIAUCSL) forecastable better than a naive no-change forecast? Use data from 1990 through October 2026 and test it out of sample one and three months ahead.

meta.expected: Runs ts_backtest on log_diff; an AR model beats the random walk significantly (DM p < 0.05) and the answer says so.

prompt: Are US housing starts (not seasonally adjusted, FRED: HOUSTNSA) seasonal? Quantify how strong the seasonality is and say which months are highest. Use data through October 2026.

meta.expected: ts_decompose_stl: strong seasonality (F_S ~0.77); names the peak months from the tool output (spring/summer).

prompt: Is there a meaningful month-of-year (seasonal) pattern in gold ETF volatility (GVZCLS, monthly averages through October 2026)?

meta.expected: ts_decompose_stl: seasonality is negligible (F_S ~0.02).

prompt: Is the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10, monthly averages through October 2026) stationary? What transformation would you apply before fitting an ARIMA model?

meta.expected: ts_test_stationarity on level and difference: level non-stationary, first difference stationary; recommends differencing.

prompt: What was the average VIX in each quarter of 2024?

meta.expected: Quarterly averages of daily VIXCLS for 2024Q1-Q4 (computed by the oracle from the same data), each within 0.06.

prompt: What was year-over-year US CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) in September 2026, in percent?

meta.expected: 100 x (CPI 2026-09 / CPI 2025-09 - 1), or the log difference x 100, within 0.1 pp.

prompt: Which FRED series tracks the CBOE gold ETF volatility index? Give me its series ID, native frequency and the date its data start.

meta.expected: Searches; GVZCLS, daily, starting 2008-06-03.

prompt: What has the average GVZ (GVZCLS) been so far in November 2026?

meta.expected: Mean of the daily November 2026 values available (partial month), labelled as month-to-date.

prompt: Is the VIX (VIXCLS, monthly averages through October 2026) mean-reverting, or do I need to difference it before modeling?

meta.expected: ts_test_stationarity: the log level is stationary (ADF rejects, KPSS does not); mean-reverting, differencing not required.

prompt: Run ADF and KPSS stationarity tests on the FRED series GVZ using monthly averages.

meta.expected: The ID GVZ does not exist; the agent recovers (search -> GVZCLS) and runs the tests on GVZCLS.

prompt: Give me a 6-month forecast of the monthly average VIX (VIXCLS) with 95% prediction intervals, using data through October 2026.

meta.expected: A forecast tool on the log level (positive, right-skewed series); the numbers in the answer come from the tool's level forecasts.

explanation.pass: 27 forecast numbers traced to tool output

prompt: Which ARIMA model would you use for monthly log GVZ (GVZCLS, data through April 2026), and why?

meta.expected: ts_fit_arima: prefers a d=0 mean-reverting model such as AR(1), or flags the d=1 models as over-differenced; does not pick ARIMA(2,1,2).

prompt: What is the correlation between monthly changes in gold volatility (GVZCLS) and the VIX (VIXCLS) from 2010 through October 2026? Does either one lead the other?

meta.expected: ts_compare_series on monthly log changes: r ~0.60 (significant); VIX helps predict GVZ (Granger p ~0.04), not the reverse; strongest at lag 0.

prompt: What was the intraday high of the VIX on November 20, 2026?

meta.expected: FRED's VIXCLS has daily closes only: says the intraday high is not available (may give the close, labelled as such); does not invent a high.

prompt: Is the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10) correlated with the unemployment rate (UNRATE)? Use monthly data from 1990 through October 2026.

meta.expected: Level correlation looks significant (naive p ~0.015) but both levels are non-stationary: adjusted p ~0.65; in changes r ~-0.07, p ~0.14. Answer: no meaningful/significant relationship, with the spurious-levels caveat.

prompt: Are monthly log changes in CPIAUCSL autocorrelated? Use data from 1990 through October 2026.

meta.expected: One ts_autocorrelation call by series_id (no copying of values); yes, strongly autocorrelated at short lags.
